chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Is'hāq ibn 'Ammār, who said:

I heard Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O group of those who became Muslims with their tongues but did not purify faith to their hearts! Do not condemn the Muslims, nor pursue their exposures (slips/flaws), for whoever pursues their exposures, Allah will pursue his exposure; and whoever Allah the Exalted pursues, He will shame him, even if he is in his own house.' From him, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abū al-Jārūd, from Abū Ja'far (peace be upon him) — similar to it.

key_terms.أَسْلَمَ بِلِسَانِهِ: became Muslim with his tongue (professed Islam)

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of exposing the flaws of other Muslims according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith highlights the spiritual danger of superficial piety, where outward profession of Islam masks a heart devoid of true faith, leading to hyper-criticism of others. The Imam warns that divine retribution for exposing others' faults is precise and inescapable, even within the privacy of one's own home, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on *satr* (concealing faults) as a key virtue of the *Momineen*. This teaching serves as a corrective to the tendency of the merely nominal believer to judge others while neglecting self-accountability.
